messages:
sam: Heads up — token-level dashboard is showing a weird front-loaded TTFT spike for /generate-chat starting ~09:10 UTC. TTFTs up ~2x on p95 but decode kernel time looks flat.

maria: hmm, do we have KV cache hitrates for those requests? Could be warmup costs or extra RPCs.

sam: perf-bot pulled a quick trace: KV hit = 98% but the first token still takes ~110ms (TTFT) while subsequent tokens are ~12-18ms.

perf-bot: Trace summary (id=trc-20260415-09:12):
```
route: /generate-chat
input_tokens: 6
kv_cache_hit: 98%
batching: auto, batch_size=1
kernel_selected: generic_ptx
kernel_time_ms: init=14 decode=11 post=2
ttft_ms: 110
per_token_decode_ms: 12
```

dez: batch_size=1 stands out. If requests are single-sample we fall back to a slower kernel path that does extra alignment. Could be kernel selection heuristic misfiring.

maria: we recently changed kernel selection thresholds in PR #4567 (lowered multi-sample threshold). Could be a regression.

sam: I ran a quick profile on a repro server (same model, cpu-bound sim):
```
# perf counters simplified
timestamp: 2026-04-15T09:14:21Z
seq_len=64 batch=1
kernel_candidates: [fast_matmul_q8, generic_ptx]
selected: generic_ptx (latency_est=95ms)
actual_decode: 11ms
extra_setup: 96ms (memory mmap + small allocs + kernel compilation cache miss)
```

jin: That "extra_setup" looks like kernel JIT or compilation cache miss. But we should not be compiling at request time for known kernels. Any eviction logs?

sam: infra logs show a kernel-cache eviction churn around 09:09 due to GC of old kernels when node memory pressure hit. That could explain the one-off frontload. But dashboard shows pattern across many nodes, not just one.

maria: maybe batching heuristics are producing many small batches on certain routes. If the route's seq_len distribution changed (longer prompts) our estimator might pick the wrong kernel. We should surface per-route seq_len histogram on the dashboard and token-indexed TTFT curve.

dez: action items I suggest: (1) add per-route kernel cache miss rate metric, (2) token-index TTFT histogram (token=0 vs token>=1), (3) annotate deploys/PRs on the dashboard so we can correlate with #4567.

sam: Agreed. Also add a small perf probe that forces batch_size=4 for a subset of traffic to test if batch aggregation removes the spike. Can be a runtime flag.

maria: I'll make a quick dashboard mockup: show p50/p95 TTFT by token_index, kernel_cache_miss_rate, batch_size distribution, kv_hit_rate. Pin time-range to the incident window.

perf-bot: Noted. Creating ticket PERF-912 with stack traces + node list.

jin: Quick note — for attribution, we should split TTFT into: kernel_load (cache miss/jit), device_enqueue, decode, postprocess, rpc. Current instrumentation lumps device_enqueue and kernel time. Need finer spans.

sam: Yep. We already have traces but span boundaries are fuzzy. I'll add explicit timing at kernel selection point and just before kernel enqueue to separate JIT from kernel exec.

dez: I'll add a small micro-benchmark that simulates eviction + single-sample routing to replicate if infra can't repro.

maria: thanks. If anyone sees similar front-load elsewhere, drop slack thread id. Also adding @oncall next. :eyes:
